info.name: NiviChat Backend API
info.description:
# NiviChat Backend

Fastify REST API for the NiviChat mobile client. A separate WebSocket process (`ws-server.js`, default port `8080`) handles real-time delivery, typing, presence, and call signaling — see the **WebSocket Reference** folder at the bottom of this collection for its event protocol; Postman requests only cover the REST surface.

## Response envelope

Every endpoint returns one of these two shapes — never a bare object/array:

**Success**
```json
{ "status": true, "message": "OK", "data": { ... }, "app_version": "2.0.11" }
```

**Error**
```json
{ "status": false, "message": "Invalid credentials", "error": null, "trace_id": "6f2b..." }
```

`trace_id` is the Fastify request id. You can force it yourself by sending an `x-trace-id` header; otherwise the server generates one.

## Auth flow

1. `POST /api/auth/register` or `POST /api/auth/login` — both return `{ accessToken, refreshToken, user }`.
2. Send `accessToken` as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every protected route (this collection does that automatically via the collection-level Bearer auth + the `{{accessToken}}` variable).
3. Access tokens are short-lived (5 minutes by default, `JWT_ACCESS_EXPIRES_IN`). When one expires you'll get **401** (never 403) — call `POST /api/auth/refresh-token` with the stored `refreshToken` to get a new pair. Refresh tokens rotate: the old one is revoked the moment you use it.
4. `POST /api/auth/logout` revokes a refresh token.

**This collection automates step 2–3's bookkeeping**: the Login, Register, and Refresh Token requests each carry a test script that saves `accessToken` / `refreshToken` / `userId` into collection variables, so every other request just works after you run one of them. Requests that also produce a `chatId`, `messageId`, or `groupId` you'll need later (List Chats, Send Message, Create Group) save those too.

## Setup

1. Import this collection **and** the companion `NiviChat-Local.postman_environment.json`.
2. Select the **NiviChat Local** environment in Postman's top-right environment picker.
3. If your server isn't on `http://localhost:3000`, edit the environment's `baseUrl` variable.
4. Run **Auth → Login** (the seed script creates `alice@nivichat.dev` / `bob@nivichat.dev` / `carol@nivichat.dev`, all with password `Password123!`, if you've run `npm run prisma:seed`). Everything else in the collection is now authenticated automatically.

## Pagination

List endpoints (`GET /api/chats/:id` messages, `GET /api/calls`) are cursor-based: pass the previous response's `nextCursor` as `?cursor=` to fetch the next page. `nextCursor` is `null` when there's nothing more.

variable.description: Set this to a second seeded user's id (e.g. bob) before running Create Direct Chat / Create Group — Users → Search Users returns ids you can copy in.

item.name: Health
item.description: Unauthenticated liveness check. Not part of `/api` — useful for confirming the server is reachable before debugging auth issues.

request.description: Returns `{ ok: true, service: "nivichat-backend" }` outside the standard envelope (this is the one route that isn't under `/api`).

item.name: Auth
item.description: Registration, login, token refresh, logout. Register and Login are the only two ways to obtain an access/refresh token pair.

request.description:
Create a new account. No auth required.

**Body**
| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `username` | string | 3-32 chars, `[a-zA-Z0-9_.]` only, unique |
| `email` | string | valid email, unique |
| `password` | string | 8-128 chars |
| `name` | string | 1-80 chars |
| `avatarUrl` | string? | valid URL |
| `deviceUniqueId` | string? | for push/device tracking |

**Response `201`**: `{ accessToken, refreshToken, user }` — `user` never includes `passwordHash`.

**Errors**: `409` if the email or username is already taken; `422` on validation failure.

Log in with either email or username. No auth required.

**Body**
| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `identifier` | string | email OR username |
| `password` | string | |
| `deviceUniqueId` | string? | if set, updates the user's stored device id |

Marks the user online (`isOnline: true`, `lastSeenAt: now`) as a side effect — this is independent of WebSocket presence, which tracks live socket connections separately.

**Response `200`**: `{ accessToken, refreshToken, user }`.

**Errors**: `401 "Invalid credentials"` for a wrong identifier/password (deliberately doesn't reveal which one was wrong).

Rotates a refresh token: the one you send is revoked and a brand-new access/refresh pair is issued. Call this when a protected request comes back `401` because the access token expired.

**Body**: `{ refreshToken }` — no `Authorization` header needed, the refresh token itself is the credential.

**Response `200`**: `{ accessToken, refreshToken }` (no `user` object this time).

**Errors**: `401` if the refresh token is invalid, expired, or already revoked (e.g. reused after a prior refresh, or after logout).

Revokes the given refresh token so it can no longer be used to mint new access tokens. Requires a valid (still-live) access token in `Authorization`.

**Body**: `{ refreshToken }`.

**Response `200`**: `data: null`.

Note: this only revokes the one refresh token you pass — if the client is logged in on multiple devices, each device's refresh token must be revoked separately (or you track/revoke them server-side by user if you need a global "log out everywhere").

item.name: Users
item.description: Current-profile management and user lookup/search. Every route here requires auth.

request.description:
Returns the caller's own profile, resolved from the access token's `sub` claim.

**Response `200`**: `PublicUser` — `{ id, username, email, name, avatarUrl, bio, isVerified, isOnline, lastSeenAt, createdAt }`. Never includes `passwordHash`.

Partial update of the caller's own profile — omit any field you don't want to change. Send `null` explicitly to clear `avatarUrl`/`bio`.

**Body** (all optional)
| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | 1-80 chars |
| `avatarUrl` | string \| null | valid URL |
| `bio` | string \| null | max 280 chars |

**Response `200`**: updated `PublicUser`.

query.description: Matched case-insensitively against username, name, and email. Omit to list all users (excluding yourself).

request.description:
Search for users to start a chat with (the mobile client's "Add Chat" screen). Always excludes the caller.

Copy an id from the response into the `otherUserId` collection variable to use it in **Chats → Create Direct Chat** or **Groups → Create Group**.

**Response `200`**: `PublicUser[]`.

Public profile lookup by id — e.g. tapping a participant's avatar inside a chat.

**Response `200`**: `PublicUser`.

**Errors**: `404` if the id doesn't exist.

item.name: Chats
item.description: List/create chats, view a chat's message history, and pin/mute/archive/leave. A "chat" is either a DIRECT (1:1) or GROUP conversation — group metadata (name, members, roles) lives under the Groups folder; this is the shared messaging container both types sit on top of.

query.description: true | false. Defaults to excluding archived chats.

request.description:
Lists every chat the caller participates in, pinned chats first, then most-recently-updated. Shaped to match the mobile client's `ChatListItem[]` directly.

Each item includes: `id`, `type` (`DIRECT`/`GROUP`), `name` and `avatarUrl` (resolved from the other participant for DIRECT, or the Group for GROUP), `otherUser` (DIRECT only, else `null`), `groupId` (GROUP only, else `null`), `isPinned`/`isMuted`/`isArchived`/`unreadCount` (per-participant state), `lastMessage` (summary, or `null` for an empty chat), `participantCount`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`.

**Response `200`**: `ChatListItem[]`.

Creates a DIRECT chat with another user, or returns the existing one if the pair already has one — idempotent by participant pair, so this is always safe to call from an "Add Chat" flow without checking first.

Run **Users → Search Users** first to populate `{{otherUserId}}`.

**Body**: `{ userId }` — the other participant's id.

**Response**: `201` (created) or `200` (already existed) with the resulting `ChatListItem`.

**Errors**: `400` if `userId` is your own id; `404` if that user doesn't exist.

query.description: A message id from a previous page's nextCursor — fetches older messages.

request.description:
Chat header (same identity fields as a `ChatListItem`, plus the full `participants` list) + a cursor-paginated page of messages, newest page first. As a side effect, marks the chat read for the caller (`unreadCount` reset to 0, `lastReadAt` updated) — calling this endpoint IS "opening the chat" from the client's perspective.

**Query**: `cursor` (optional, a message id — paginate older messages), `limit` (1-100, default 30).

**Response `200`**: `{ chat, messages: MessageDTO[], nextCursor }`. `nextCursor` is `null` once you've reached the oldest message.

**Errors**: `404` if you're not a participant of this chat (same response whether the chat doesn't exist or you're just not in it, to avoid leaking existence).

Updates the caller's own per-chat state — pin/mute/archive are per-participant, not global to the chat (muting a group only silences it for you).

**Body** (send at least one)
| Field | Type |
|---|---|
| `isPinned` | boolean |
| `isMuted` | boolean |
| `isArchived` | boolean |

**Response `200`**: `{ isPinned, isMuted, isArchived }`.

Removes the caller from this chat. If you were the last remaining participant, the chat (and its messages) is deleted outright.

For a GROUP chat this is equivalent to leaving the group as an ordinary member — if you're the group's only admin, prefer **Groups → Disband Group** or promote someone else first, since this endpoint doesn't reassign the admin role.

**Response `200`**: `data: null`.

item.name: Messages
item.description: Send, fetch, edit, and delete messages, plus per-recipient read-receipt status. Sending here (REST) and sending over the WebSocket's `message:send` event both go through the same persistence path and both broadcast `message:new` — use whichever fits your client better.

request.description:
Sends a message into a chat you participate in. Persists it, creates a `SENT` receipt for every other participant, bumps the chat's `updatedAt` and their `unreadCount`, and broadcasts `message:new` over WebSocket to every connected participant (including your own other devices).

**Body**
| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `chatId` | string | required |
| `type` | enum | `TEXT` \| `IMAGE` \| `AUDIO` \| `FILE` \| `VIDEO` \| `VIDEO_CALL` \| `VOICE_CALL`, default `TEXT` |
| `text` | string? | 1-4000 chars; **required if `type` is `TEXT`** |
| `replyToId` | string? | must be a message id already in this chat |
| `attachments` | array? | max 10, see shape below — upload each file via `POST /api/attachments` first and pass its returned `url`/`type`/etc. here |

Each `attachments[]` entry: `{ type: IMAGE\|AUDIO\|FILE\|VIDEO, url, fileName?, fileSize?, width?, height?, duration?, waveform?, thumbnail? }`.

**Response `201`**: full `MessageDTO` (`{ id, chatId, senderId, sender, type, text, replyToId, isEdited, editedAt, isDeleted, deletedAt, createdAt, attachments, reactions }`).

**Errors**: `404` if you're not a participant; `400` if `replyToId` points to a message in a different chat.

Fetches a single message. You must be a participant of the chat it belongs to.

**Response `200`**: `MessageDTO`.

**Errors**: `404` if the message doesn't exist or you're not in its chat.

This one endpoint (`PATCH /api/messages/:id`) handles three different actions via the `action` discriminator — this request shows `edit`; see **Delete Message (via action)** and **Update Message Receipt Status** for the other two. Only the original sender can edit or delete; sets `isEdited: true` and stamps `editedAt`. Broadcasts `message:update` over WebSocket (an extension beyond the documented WS event set, added so real-time clients see edits/deletes too).

**Body**: `{ action: "edit", text }` — `text` 1-4000 chars.

**Response `200`**: updated `MessageDTO`.

**Errors**: `403` if you're not the sender; `400` if the message was already deleted.

Soft-deletes the message (`isDeleted: true`, `text` cleared) via the same action-discriminated PATCH as Edit. The row is kept (so replies referencing it don't break), just its content is cleared. Only the sender can do this.

See also **Delete Message (plain DELETE)** below — a REST-idiomatic alias for clients that prefer a plain `DELETE` verb over `PATCH` + `action`. Both do exactly the same thing.

**Body**: `{ action: "delete" }`.

**Response `200`**: the now soft-deleted `MessageDTO` (`text: null`, `isDeleted: true`).

Upserts **your own** delivery/read receipt for this message — unlike edit/delete, this doesn't require being the sender (it's the recipient reporting their own status). This is the REST equivalent of the WebSocket `message:read` event, useful for clients that aren't holding a live socket.

**Body**: `{ action: "status", status }` — `status` one of `SENDING` \| `SENT` \| `DELIVERED` \| `SEEN` \| `READ` \| `MISSED`.

**Response `200`**: the `MessageReceipt` row `{ id, messageId, userId, status, updatedAt }`.

Plain-REST alias for `PATCH { action: "delete" }` — same soft-delete behavior, sender-only. Prefer this if your HTTP client library makes `DELETE` more natural than a discriminated `PATCH` body.

**Response `200`**: `data: null` (or `"Message already deleted"` if it already was — this call is idempotent).

item.name: Groups
item.description: Group chat creation and membership management. Every GROUP chat has a backing Chat row (see the Chats folder for messaging on it) plus this Group/GroupMember metadata for name/avatar/description/roles.

request.description:
Creates a GROUP chat in one call: the backing Chat, a ChatParticipant row for you and every member, and the Group + GroupMember rows (you become `ADMIN`, everyone else `MEMBER`).

Run **Users → Search Users** first to populate `{{otherUserId}}`, or edit the body to list multiple ids directly.

**Body**
| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | 1-80 chars |
| `avatarUrl` | string? | valid URL |
| `description` | string? | max 280 chars |
| `memberIds` | string[] | 1-256 ids; your own id is filtered out automatically if included |

**Response `201`**: `GroupDTO` — `{ id, chatId, name, avatarUrl, description, createdBy, createdAt, members: [{ userId, role, joinedAt, user }] }`. Use `data.chatId` to send messages into the group (via the Chats/Messages endpoints).

Group metadata + full member list with roles. Any member (not just admins) can view this.

**Response `200`**: `GroupDTO`.

**Errors**: `404` if the group doesn't exist or you're not a member.

Updates the group's name/avatar/description. **Admin only.**

**Body** (send at least one, `null` clears `avatarUrl`/`description`)
| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string? | 1-80 chars |
| `avatarUrl` | string \| null | valid URL |
| `description` | string \| null | max 280 chars |

**Response `200`**: updated `GroupDTO`.

**Errors**: `403` if you're a member but not an admin.

Adds new members as `MEMBER` role. **Admin only.** IDs already in the group are silently skipped rather than erroring — safe to call with an overlapping list.

**Body**: `{ userIds }` — 1-256 ids.

**Response `200`**: updated `GroupDTO` (message is `"No new members to add"` if every id was already a member).

**Errors**: `403` if not an admin; `400` if any id doesn't correspond to a real user.

query.description: The member to remove. Pass your own userId to leave the group instead.

request.description:
Removes a member from the group (deletes their GroupMember and ChatParticipant rows). Admins can remove anyone; a non-admin member can only pass their own `userId` — i.e. this doubles as "leave group" when `userId` equals the caller.

**Response `200`**: `data: null`, message `"Left group"` or `"Member removed"` depending on who was removed.

**Errors**: `403` if you try to remove someone else without being an admin; `404` if the target isn't a member.

Permanently deletes the group: the backing Chat is removed, which cascades to Group, GroupMember, ChatParticipant, Message, and Call rows for it. **Admin only. Not reversible.**

**Response `200`**: `data: null`.

**Errors**: `403` if you're not an admin.

item.name: Attachments
item.description: File uploads for use in messages. Upload first, then reference the returned url/type/etc. in a message's `attachments[]`.

request.description:
Multipart upload — stores the file under `public/uploads/<uuid>.<ext>` and serves it statically at the returned `url`. This endpoint only stores the file and returns its metadata; it does **not** attach it to a message by itself — copy the response fields into a subsequent `POST /api/messages` call's `attachments[]` array.

**Body**: `multipart/form-data` with a single field named `file`. In Postman: Body tab → `form-data` → key `file` → change the type dropdown from "Text" to "File" → choose a file.

`type` in the response is inferred from the upload's MIME prefix: `image/*` → `IMAGE`, `audio/*` → `AUDIO`, `video/*` → `VIDEO`, anything else → `FILE`.

**Response `201`**: `{ url, type, fileName, fileSize }`.

**Errors**: `400` if the `file` field is missing or the file is empty; `413` if it exceeds 25MB.

item.name: Calls
item.description: Call history logging. This is a record-keeping endpoint — the actual WebRTC audio/video signaling (offer/answer/ICE) happens over the WebSocket `call:signal`/`call:incoming` events, not REST.

request.description:
Logs a call against a chat you participate in — call this once the call ends (or is missed/declined) to record it in history.

**Body**
| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `chatId` | string | required |
| `type` | enum | `VOICE` \| `VIDEO` |
| `status` | enum | `MISSED` \| `COMPLETED` \| `DECLINED` |
| `startedAt` | string? | ISO 8601 datetime, defaults to now |
| `endedAt` | string? | ISO 8601 datetime |
| `duration` | integer? | seconds, >= 0 |

**Response `201`**: `CallDTO` — `{ id, chatId, initiatorId, initiator, type, status, startedAt, endedAt, duration }`.

**Errors**: `404` if you're not a participant of `chatId`.

query.description: A call id from a previous page's nextCursor.

request.description:
Call history across every chat the caller participates in, newest first, cursor-paginated.

**Response `200`**: `{ calls: CallDTO[], nextCursor }`.

item.name: WebSocket Reference (docs only, no requests)
item.description:
The real-time layer lives in a separate process (`ws-server.js`, default `ws://localhost:8080`) — plain WebSocket, not REST, so it isn't represented as runnable Postman requests here. If your Postman version supports WebSocket requests, connect to `{{wsUrl}}` (add that variable yourself) and send JSON frames shaped `{ "event": string, "data": object }`.

**Handshake**: first frame after connecting must be `{ "event": "auth", "data": { "token": "<accessToken>" } }` within 5 seconds, or the server closes the connection. Reuse the same access token this collection uses for REST.

**Client → Server events**
| Event | Payload | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `auth` | `{ token }` | Authenticates the socket |
| `message:send` | `{ chatId, type, text, replyToId?, attachments? }` | Same persistence as `POST /api/messages`, broadcasts `message:new` |
| `typing:start` / `typing:stop` | `{ chatId }` | Broadcasts `typing:update` to other participants |
| `message:read` | `{ chatId, messageId }` | Marks your receipt `SEEN`, resets your unread count |
| `presence:ping` | `{}` | Heartbeat, updates `lastSeenAt` |
| `call:signal` | `{ chatId, toUserId, type, payload }` | WebRTC offer/answer/ICE relay — `type: "offer"` reaches the callee as `call:incoming`, everything else as `call:signal` |

**Server → Client events**: `auth` (handshake ack), `message:new`, `message:status` (`{ messageId, userId, status }` — `DELIVERED` when a connected recipient receives it in real time, `SEEN` after `message:read`), `message:update` (edit/delete), `typing:update`, `presence:update` (`{ userId, isOnline, lastSeenAt }`, deduplicated so you get exactly one per contact even if you share multiple chats with them), `call:incoming`, `call:signal`, `error` (`{ message, code }`).
